stem: While documenting the transaction, a patient requests transfer of an unfilled electronic Sonata prescription to a second DEA-registered retail pharmacy. Both pharmacists can communicate directly. What else matters?

choices.text: Confirm it has not been transferred before, remains electronic and unaltered, and state law permits the transfer.
Transfer any unfilled Sonata prescription even if it began on paper after documenting whether the federal pathway applied to paper and fax prescriptions.
Permit repeated transfers until the first dispensing.
Let a technician transmit the record without pharmacist communication.
Ignore Massachusetts transfer restrictions because federal permission preempts every state condition.

explanation.core_reasoning: 'Confirm it has not been transferred before, remains electronic and unaltered, and state law permits the transfer.' is the governing result. By contrast, 'Transfer any unfilled Sonata prescription even if it began on paper.' would require that the federal pathway applied to paper and fax prescriptions. The decisive cue appears in 'While documenting the transaction, a patient requests transfer of an unfilled electronic Sonata prescription to a second DEA-registered retail pharmacy. Both pharmacists can communicate directly. What else matters?'.

choice_analysis.A: 'Confirm it has not been transferred before, remains electronic and unaltered, and state law permits the transfer.': supported by electronic prescriptions.
choice_analysis.B: 'Transfer any unfilled Sonata prescription even if it began on paper.' would apply only if the federal pathway applied to paper and fax prescriptions; 'While documenting the transaction, a patient requests transfer of an unfilled electronic Sonata prescription to a second DEA-registered retail pharmacy. Both pharmacists can communicate directly. What else matters?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.C: 'Permit repeated transfers until the first dispensing.' would apply only if the rule allowed more than one transfer; 'While documenting the transaction, a patient requests transfer of an unfilled electronic Sonata prescription to a second DEA-registered retail pharmacy. Both pharmacists can communicate directly. What else matters?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.D: 'Let a technician transmit the record without pharmacist communication.' would apply only if the required direct communication could be delegated entirely; 'While documenting the transaction, a patient requests transfer of an unfilled electronic Sonata prescription to a second DEA-registered retail pharmacy. Both pharmacists can communicate directly. What else matters?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.E: 'Ignore Massachusetts transfer restrictions because federal permission preempts every state condition.' would apply only if federal permission operated without the state-law prerequisite; 'While documenting the transaction, a patient requests transfer of an unfilled electronic Sonata prescription to a second DEA-registered retail pharmacy. Both pharmacists can communicate directly. What else matters?' states otherwise.

related_facts: zaleplon (Sonata) is used for short-term treatment of insomnia; it is federal Schedule IV and Massachusetts Schedule IV.

At a patient's request, an unfilled electronic Schedule II through V prescription may be transferred once between DEA-registered retail pharmacies if allowed by state law, kept electronic, unaltered, and communicated directly between pharmacists.

Match the scenario's operative facts to One-time transfer of electronic controlled prescriptions
